title: sdm-client Rust core quirk register
description: Every behavior of the reference the Rust core keeps, drops or changes by recorded decision (migration-plan.md section 5). Format 2 (Phase 1 decision A6, T1.14): per-case old and new outcomes, and decision references into any phase's decisions file. scripts/rust_core/register.py validate holds the file to this schema and to the rules a schema cannot state.

outcome.description: A case's projected outcome as ratchet.py writes it: 'success' or 'refusal <CODE>', then ' at <stage>' and ' (<exception class>)' where the runner observes them; 'none' where the checkpoint holds no baseline, 'removed' and 'diagnostic' for a case taken out of acceptance.

case.description: The line's key, as the observation schema's key: the bare case ID on DuckDB, <case>@sqlite or <case>@postgres on another database (T2.0f); the part before @ a corpus case.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique in the file; never reused, so an entry is never deleted (a withdrawn one is rejected).

kind.description: keep: the core reproduces the reference; drop: the core stops reproducing a reference accident; change: the core (or the reference) answers differently from the old behavior.

cases.description: Contract case IDs, or for an entry written before the corpus the legacy form: a task ID (T<phase>.<n> and a letter) or a Phase 1b inventory case ID.

refs.description: What an entry cites that is not a case: Phase 0 vector groups, commits of the reference, documents, other register entries.

case_outcomes.description: Generated by ratchet.py from the observations, never written by hand: each case, cell and runner whose projected outcome the entry changes, with the exact old and new outcome.

approved_by.description: Who approved the entry, or for a rejected entry who rejected it; null while proposed. The reviewer approves; owner records only the owner's own written answer. An entry that refuses an input the reference accepts needs owner.

decision_ref.description: The decisions row that covers the entry, if one does: the decisions file by its path in the repository and the row's ID (a number in Phase 0, a letter and a number from Phase 1).
